html:
The Tataviam are a Native people of the upper Santa Clara River and the Santa Clarita Valley, in the hills north of the San Fernando Valley in what is now Los Angeles County, California.

They probably spoke a Uto-Aztecan language, though it is poorly known. Their neighbours were the Tongva, the Kitanemuk, the Chumash and the Serrano. After Mission San Fernando was founded in 1797, the mission drew in most Tataviam, and their descendants took the name Fernandeño. The tribe today is not federally recognised.
